context_switch.note: One of the three that touch no Lua. Together with `exception` and `ipc_roundtrip` they are the control group: all three were identical to three decimals across taking the interpreter out of the kernel, which is the evidence that the kernel itself did not change.
context_switch.unit: counter ticks per operation, QEMU -icount shift=0

exception.unit: counter ticks per operation, QEMU -icount shift=0

gc_pause_max.note: The worst single collector step, measured in a process. 78221, drifting up with what the process carries in the same way serialize does and by far less: 78129 before gfx, 78199 after, 78221 with the font. A long step is dominated by the 3000-object heap the benchmark builds rather than by a handful of library tables. Before that it was 77860, running inside the kernel with interrupts masked. Leaving EL1 cost the interpreter +0.3% and nothing else: a collector step costs the same at either privilege level. Interrupts are live in the window now, because a process cannot mask them, and for a pause metric that is more honest rather than less - a pause the user feels includes the tick that landed in it.
gc_pause_max.unit: counter ticks per operation, QEMU -icount shift=0

ipc_roundtrip.note: A minimal message: the floor of the IPC path, including the capability translation every delivery performs. Compare with `serialize`, which is what carrying a real Lua table costs on top - about forty-seven times more. 30.000 -> 31.001 when a capability slot gained a kind. A slot used to hold an endpoint and nothing else, so `resolve` could go straight to the pointer; it holds either an endpoint or a region of memory now, so every resolve loads the tag and compares it first, and a round trip resolves twice. That is the price of two kinds in one table and it is not avoidable while indices stay the only way to name anything - the alternative is a second table with a second index space, which is the global-name design this kernel does not have. Measured, not estimated: 31.001 to three decimals on three consecutive builds. `context_switch` and `exception` did not move at all across the same change, which is what says the cost is in the capability lookup and not in the path around it.
ipc_roundtrip.unit: counter ticks per operation, QEMU -icount shift=0

serialize.note: Best of five processes within a run. **This benchmark is sensitive to what else is in the process, not only to the serialiser.** 1364.9 -> 1394.1 when the gfx library started being opened in every process, and 1394.1 -> 1412.5 when the 1.5 KB font array joined it, and 1412.5 -> 1450.6 when shared memory added `sys.memory`, `sys.memory_map`, `sys.memory_size` and `gfx.wrap` to every process. The serialiser has not changed once across either. The cause is measured, not guessed: the same tree with the requiref for gfx commented out gives 1358.2. More objects and more image on a 2 MB heap means the collector paces differently through the measured loop. So: if this moves and nothing in serialize.c or sys_user.c did, look at what was added to the user image. It will drift again with the next library. Making it independent of the process it runs in - a fixed GC pause setting and a forced collection before the loop - is a known improvement and is not done. Spread: consecutive runs of one recorded image have spanned 0.045%; across separately built images of the same source, up to 1.1%. Before all this it was 1037.6, when it measured serialize_pack/unpack called from C inside the kernel. It measures sys.pack/sys.unpack from a process now, which allocates a Lua string per round where the C version wrote into a struct message. Those are not comparable.
serialize.unit: counter ticks per operation, QEMU -icount shift=0
